runs.name: S&P Global Inc.
runs.box: OUT AT Q6, ON THE NARROWER STOP (ALL-STOCK DEAL IN UNDERVALUED STOCK)
runs.entry: Price **$407.82** (close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged) x **294.8M shares** (10-Q cover as of 2026-07-24, 0000064040-26-000045, excluding 7.2M held by the Markit Group Holdings Limited Employee Benefit Trust; cover_shares.py agreed) = cap **$120.2B**; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y). Primary document the FY2025 10-K (0000064040-26-000013, filed 2026-02-11), with the 10-Q for 2026-06-30, the 8-K of 2026-07-02 (0001104659-26-080005, Mobility spun off 2026-07-01) and its 8-K/A with the pro forma restatement. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs. Q1 IN on the deciding part (Ratings, 45.2% of 2021-2025 segment operating profit, 48.6% without the 2022 divestiture gain; margin 45%, 40%, 39% through 2007-2009). Q2 IN on the deciding part: Ratings margin 44% (2015) to 64% (2025), 55% at the 2022 trough; issuers kept paying after about $1.6B of settlements; Moody's MIS a near-twin (51.8% to 63.6% adjusted, 2018-2025), MSCI 42% to 55%, FactSet about 31% to 32% (2016-2025); Fitch, Bloomberg, LSEG and Argus not SEC filers, the 10-K's competition text names no rival. Q3 weighed (for on the business, against on the merger's return). Q4 no STOP (guidance and an adjusted EPS beside GAAP weigh mildly against). Q5 integrity IN on the present managers, the 2015 DOJ and states settlement ($1.375B), the SEC's 2015 Section 17(a)(1) finding on 2011 CMBS ratings and the 2024 $20M recordkeeping penalty carried, the issuer-pays incentive carried; the analyst notes a stricter reader could close at Q5. **Q6 narrower STOP fired:** IHS Markit bought wholly in stock (113.8M shares at $380.89, about $43.5B, FY2022 10-K) while SPGI's own no-growth value on Q7's construction at the deal date's 2.29% sovereign was $474.73 a share (the stock given at about 0.80 of its own bottom); IHS Markit paid at 1.17 times its own no-growth value; holders gave 32.1% of the combined company for 23% to 25% of its owner cash. The box named OUT by a CONVENTION of the run (the STOP does not name its box). Q7 to Q12 not reached. Beneath the stop, COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash all-equity, Mobility removed by estimate, $4,126M / $1,958M / $2,873M / $4,778M / $4,621M for 2021-2025, literal mean $3,671M, central base $4,090M (2023-2025, the years the filer restated to today's perimeter, a CONVENTION of the run); range **$216.63-$565.06** all-equity ($229.61-$552.50 equity-only; literal window $191.23-$503.95); fair **$187.97** all-equity ($203.06 equity-only; literal $165.52); the price inside the range, the top case earning about 7.3% at the price. Balance sheets FY2016-FY2025: equity near zero before 2022 on buybacks, $36.4B after the stock issued; goodwill and intangibles $52.7B, tangible equity negative; long-term debt $3.6B to $12.4B; unearned revenue $4.1B funds working capital; capital spending about 1% of revenue. Strongest against: owner cash per share up about 2.4% a year 2021-2025 despite $23.6B of buybacks at $342-$519, above any computed bottom, with more than $7B planned for 2026; pay on adjusted measures with no capital charge; the CME put on the Indices stake carried at $4.9B against about $4.0B of cash. Could not get: Mobility's own cash flow (estimated), IHS Markit's January-February 2022 (never filed), a maintenance split of capital spending; Market Intelligence not separated at no growth in Q7 (the analyst's own gap). Analyst's framework gaps for the operator: (1) Q6's narrower STOP has no method for intrinsic value of a past deal (sovereign range or ten-percent floor; on the floor it would not fire and the file would close OUT at Q7 on the floor anyway), no time limit (the merger was signed in 2020 under an earlier chief executive) and no box; (2) the parts rule lets a part with 45% to 49% of profit decide; (3) no treatment for a non-deciding part that is TOO HARD; (4) the five-year window across a merger, a later spin-off and unfiled target months; (5) the template has no slot for a weighing question's narrower STOP. Contamination declared by the analyst: a first directory listing filtered on the ticker printed the names of two earlier SPGI run files and a research folder, none opened; recorded as a breach of the rule's spirit. Eight commits (6570ac2c to cfb28198), one per question. Dispatcher quote check: 64 quoted fragments beside ids, 52 in their rows; the 12 others are filer or rival-filer quotes attributed to the filer in the text and set before a cited rule, not offered as the rows' words; no slip found; recorded, not fixed. No alert (box not OUT at Q7 or IN); v4.1 bands retired (2). Position note filled at the fold: not held. check_framework PASS.
runs.narr: Q6 narrower STOP: the IHS Markit merger was paid wholly in SPGI stock at about 0.80 of the bottom of SPGI's own range at the 2022 sovereign, holders giving 32.1% of the combined company for 23% to 25% of its owner cash; Q1 and Q2 IN on Ratings, Q5 integrity IN with the settlements carried. Beneath the stop, range $216.63-$565.06 all-equity, fair $187.97 against $407.82. Five framework gaps reported, chief among them that Q6's STOP names no method, no time limit and no box.
